objective: Keep Hspec, QuickCheck, and IHP test support in development without direct production app-library declarations

transitive_inspection.QuickCheck: Retained transitively by aeson in the production derivation closure, but not declared by app-lib and not imported by production source.
transitive_inspection.hspec: Retained transitively by the monolithic ihp library in the production derivation closure, but no Hspec family package is declared by app-lib and no Hspec interface is imported by production source.
transitive_inspection.ihp-hspec: Absent from the candidate production derivation closure.
transitive_inspection.decision: Do not claim that moving three direct packages removes every test-named transitive store path. The generated app-lib declaration and direct Nix inputs are the boundary changed here; issue 349 owns general production dependency narrowing.

matched_12_core_profile.interpretation: The durable improvement is 129.36 MB less app-library closure and three fewer direct Nix inputs. Module/interface counts are unchanged, as expected. Matched builder peak RSS improved 12.25%, CPU 4.02%, and wall 9.37%; cgroup peak growth worsened 5.52%. Swap crossed zero, so no percentage is claimed. The conflicting host-wide cgroup sample is retained rather than hidden.

optimized_runtime.interpretation: The statically linked runtime closure is effectively unchanged; test dependencies retained by aeson and ihp remain transitive. The app-library build closure, not runtime behavior, is the accepted seam.
